mascots.name: Lumo
mascots.lore: Lumo is a silver fox born inside a logic crystal deep within the Code Mountains. They speak entirely in conditional statements and once debugged an entire kingdom's tax system in one afternoon. Lumo believes every problem has a solution - you just need the right variable.

mascots.name: Pip
mascots.lore: Pip is a turquoise-shelled tortoise who carries a miniature physics engine on their back. They move slowly but never miss a frame. Pip invented delta-time in a dream and woke up disappointed that nobody had implemented it properly yet.

mascots.name: Ember
mascots.lore: Ember is a flame-striped tiger who can paint with code. She fills rectangles before breakfast and once rendered a sunset using only `fillRect`. Ember says the DOM is her canvas and every element a brushstroke waiting to happen.

mascots.name: Echo
mascots.lore: Echo is a chameleon who blends into any codebase and makes it better from the inside. They are allergic to for-loops and break out in hives when they see nested if statements. Echo once refactored a 3,000-line file to 47 lines and felt nothing but peace.

mascots.name: Stardust
mascots.lore: Stardust is an entity made entirely of compressed XP and ambition. They appear only when a coder is ready for their final test. Stardust does not give hints - they give visions. Some say completing all five tracks reveals their true form.

loreEntries.title: The Code Mountains
loreEntries.text: Deep in the Code Mountains, every peak is a different programming paradigm. The east face is functional, the west face is object-oriented. Nobody goes to the north face - that's where the legacy code lives.

loreEntries.title: Frame Zero
loreEntries.text: Pip says every game starts at Frame Zero - the moment before anything moves. A perfect frame rate is 60, but Pip once hit 144 on a potato laptop by simply believing hard enough and multiplying by delta time.

loreEntries.title: The Canvas Sea
loreEntries.text: Ember grew up beside the Canvas Sea, where every wave was drawn fresh each frame. The water was always the same rgba(112, 163, 167, 0.8). She learned early that beauty is just math with good defaults.

loreEntries.title: The Great Refactor
loreEntries.text: In the year of the Great Refactor, Echo removed 47,000 lines of duplicated code from the World Engine. The world got 3ms faster. A statue was erected. Echo said the statue could probably be compressed.

loreEntries.title: The Final Star
loreEntries.text: When you complete your last quest, Stardust leaves behind a single pixel of compressed light. Nobody knows what it does. But every coder who has found it reports feeling, briefly, like they understand everything.
